title: Rollout: canary overload protection in us-east for 1–2 models, evaluate impact, then expand globally
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Roll out the Hosted overload protection stack (gateway admission control + routing breaker evaluation + runtime bounded queues/shed points) via a controlled canary in us-east for 1–2 models, validate customer impact + SLO accounting, then expand to additional models/regions with clear rollback criteria.

Why
We need deterministic overload behavior (429/503 w/ stable Redwood error codes + Retry-After) without introducing new failure modes (breaker flapping, retry storms, streaming disconnect regressions). A staged rollout is required to confirm:
- Tail latency stability during spikes (p95/p99) improves vs baseline
- Internal 5xx/timeouts drop without shifting failures to ambiguous client experience
- SDK/OpenAI-compat error shape is consistent across endpoints
- Oncall paging rules + SLO toolkit treat load-shed as “overload-protected” (not internal incident-worthy) per policy

Scope
Phase A (Canary, us-east)
- Enable overload protection feature flags in us-east only
- Canary on 1–2 models (proposed: a high-traffic general model + one long-context heavy model)
- Start at low exposure (e.g., 1–5% of Hosted traffic for those models), then ramp
- Verify dashboards/alerts, incident-bot snapshots, and runbook steps

Phase B (Expand, us-east)
- Expand to remaining top models in us-east (prioritize highest QPS routes first)
- Validate no disproportionate tier impact (fairness / no starvation)

Phase C (Global expansion)
- Expand region-by-region (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) once canary meets criteria
- Keep region-specific safe defaults (thresholds/hysteresis) and maintain an emergency disable toggle

Rollout plan (executed)
1) Pre-flight checklist (must be green)
- Dashboard panels available + reviewed: admission rate, shed rate, breaker state transitions, queue depth, 429/503 breakdown by route/model/tier, streaming disconnects
- Alerting in “observe only” for canary start (no paging on expected 429/503 increases)
- Error taxonomy live in gateway + OpenAI-compat mapping validated (headers, Retry-After, stable JSON shape)
- Runtime bounded queue enabled behind flags; shed reasons plumbed end-to-end in logs/traces
- Runbook published + oncall permissions confirmed for config changes

2) Canary start (us-east)
- Enable flags for two models in us-east at 1% traffic
- Hold 60–90 minutes, confirm breaker transitions behave and no control plane degradation
- Ramp to 5%, then 10%, then 25% based on criteria below

3) Canary evaluation criteria (must meet for 24 hours at >=10% exposure)
Success metrics
- p99 latency during known spike windows improves by >=15% vs baseline week, without raising p50 materially (<=5% regression)
- Reduced internal 5xx/timeouts attributable to overload by >=30% in us-east for canary models
- 429/503 responses are dominated by Redwood overload codes (not random 502/504); Retry-After present in >=99% of overload responses
- No sustained increase in streaming disconnect rate; if disconnects rise, verify it correlates with deliberate overload shed behavior and is documented
Safety metrics / guardrails
- Breaker flapping rate below threshold (no more than 3 open/close transitions per (model,tier) per hour under steady load)
- No evidence of client retry storm (request rate amplification <= 1.1x during recovery windows)
- Dedicated traffic unaffected (flags scoped to Hosted), and Shared control-plane remains responsive

4) Rollback criteria (immediate)
- Control plane saturation or routing service elevated error rate correlated with breaker evaluation
- Breaker flapping causing instability (open/close loops) leading to higher internal 5xx than baseline
- Incorrect HTTP mapping / missing Retry-After / malformed error payload causing client crashes
- Material increase in SDK-reported “unknown error” or OpenAI-compat schema regressions
Rollback actions
- Flip regional master flag off (us-east)
- If needed, disable per-model flag only and retain observability
- Post in #eng-releases and #incidents with timestamp + snapshot

Owners / involved
- Release coordination: Connor O'Brien
- SRE: Rafael Mendes (rollout approval), Christine Wong (breaker behavior)
- Platform/Routing: Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon
- API Gateway: Amara Diallo
- Runtime: Lena Fischer / Samir Qureshi
- Observability: Sergio Costa
- Product sign-off (customer behavior): Nikhil Sharma / Henry Cho

Implementation artifacts
- Feature-flag rollout controls: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18502
- Dashboard + alert rules: https://github.com/redwood/observability-pack/pull/611
- SLO toolkit accounting (overload-protected errors): https://github.com/redwood/slo-toolkit/pull/204
- Perf canary overload scenarios: https://github.com/redwood/perf-canary/pull/97

Outcome / notes (final)
- Canary executed in us-east on 2 models (one high-QPS chat route + one long-context heavy route).
- After initial ramp, discovered breaker cooldown edge case causing elevated transition rate; mitigated via hotfix and cooldown tuning.
- Post-hotfix, canary met success criteria at 25% exposure for 48 hours and then expanded to all top Hosted models in us-east.
- Global rollout proceeded region-by-region with a 24-hour hold between regions; no Sev1/Sev2 incidents during rollout window.

Follow-ups
- ENG-4840: alert tuning after real-world canary data (reduce noise / flapping sensitivity)
- ENG-4841: post-launch review comparing incident rate + customer tickets pre/post rollout

Notes for Support/CS
If customers ask about new 429/503 behavior, refer them to updated retry guidance: exponential backoff with jitter; respect Retry-After; avoid immediate retry loops on streaming reconnect.

2025-12-12 (Sergio Costa): Dashboard panels ready in staging. Please ensure we do not label metrics by request_id; keep labels to model, region, tier, route_group only. Added an annotation panel for breaker open events.
2025-12-13 (Rafael Mendes): Approving canary start once PR-18502 is merged + the emergency regional disable toggle is verified on prod. Also: page on internal 5xx spike, not on 429/503 spike.
2025-12-16 (Christine Wong): Canary started us-east @1% for model A/B. Observed elevated breaker transitions (cooldown too short) under burst test. Not rolling forward until fixed.
2025-12-18 (Connor O'Brien): Rolled out hotfix from breaker cooldown adjustment and re-ran canary. Breaker transitions stabilized; ramped to 10%. No control plane regression seen.
2025-12-20 (Henry Cho): Reviewed customer-facing errors from canary. Retry-After present and error codes match ADR. Please ensure status page template is ready before global expansion.
2026-01-06 (Connor O'Brien): us-east expanded to 100% for top models. Proceeding to eu-west canary tomorrow with same ramp schedule and 24h hold.

2026-01-22 (Connor O'Brien): Global rollout complete (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast). Master flags remain scoped to Hosted. Creating a separate ticket for long-term policy tuning + post-launch review inputs.
